concerns.concern: The temperature series has no data between 150 and 200 K, so the velocity drop cannot be pinned to T_N. It could have started anywhere above about 155 K, including as a precursor in the paramagnetic phase.
concerns.quote: There are no measurements between 150 and 200 K, so the 'drop at T_N' is a single interval of 50 K.

concerns.concern: The 5.5% softening compares the single highest paramagnetic point (200 K) with the antiferromagnetic data, and no anharmonic background is fitted. Measured from the 300 K value, the softening is only about 2.7%.
concerns.quote: The 5.5% figure is measured from the PM maximum rather than from an extrapolated background.

concerns.concern: The room-temperature velocity at the same wavevector differs by about 4% between Fig. 3b (~1945 m/s) and Fig. 4 (~1865 m/s). Measurement reproducibility is therefore comparable to the claimed magnetic effect.
concerns.quote: This ~4% discrepancy between nominally identical measurements is close to the 5.5% magnetic softening being claimed.

concerns.concern: DFT/FEM give only a 0.54% frequency shift, about 10 times smaller than measured. Yet the abstract says the calculations 'reproduce' the magnetic-order-induced shift.
concerns.quote: DFT gives a 0.54% shift, ~10× smaller than measured

concerns.concern: The known temperature dependence of the SiO2/Si substrate, and thermal-mismatch strain in the film, are not controlled for. Part of the velocity change may therefore be substrate-driven rather than magnetoelastic.
concerns.quote: The paper measures the bare substrate only at RT (Supplementary Fig. 5) and has no non-magnetic reference film.

concerns.concern: The inferred shear softening conflicts with the DFT results. DFT leaves c44, one of the two constants the Rayleigh mode is most sensitive to, unchanged. The highlighted c66 change should barely affect a sagittal Rayleigh wave.
concerns.quote: In Table 1, c44 is identical in NM and AFM (9.7 GPa), and c55 slightly increases.

concerns.concern: The estimate Δc/c ≈ 2Δv/v assumes a homogeneous half-space and ignores the mode's substantial weight in the substrate. The 11% figure therefore underestimates the NiPS3 softening required.
concerns.quote: A 5.5% velocity drop therefore requires more than 11% softening of the relevant NiPS3 constants.

concerns.concern: A non-spin-polarized DFT state is a poor proxy for the paramagnet, which retains local Ni moments. The NM–AFM difference then mainly reflects moment formation rather than magnetic ordering.
concerns.quote: A non-spin-polarized calculation quenches the moments entirely, changing Ni–S bonding, volume and the electronic structure.

concerns.concern: No Hubbard U is used or mentioned in the DFT. Plain GGA poorly describes NiPS3's Mott-like gap and moment-dependent bonding.
concerns.quote: the Methods list plain PBE-D3 with no +U.

concerns.concern: The paper states antiferromagnetic interlayer coupling, which contradicts the propagation vector k=[010] (implying ferromagnetic stacking). If the DFT supercell used interlayer AFM, the computed tensor corresponds to the wrong magnetic structure.
concerns.quote: Stating AFM interlayer coupling contradicts the quoted k.

concerns.concern: The magnetoelastic renormalization formula is unjustified and internally inconsistent. It uses a single-ion-like coupling while being called exchange striction, and it relies on the uniform rather than staggered susceptibility. No coupling constants are estimated, so the claimed quantitative link is unsupported.
concerns.quote: The claim that this 'quantitatively links' the macroscopic softening to exchange striction is therefore not supported.

concerns.concern: The optical-phonon frequency shift is written in terms of the first derivative of the exchange integral. The frequency shift should depend on the second derivative; the first derivative gives a static displacement.
concerns.quote: The stated Δω_opt ∝ (∂J_ij/∂u_α)⟨S_i·S_j⟩ is therefore incorrect as a formula for the frequency shift.

concerns.concern: Key Brillouin-scattering details are missing, including laser power, spot size and heating, cryostat and sensor location, polarization, free spectral range, acquisition time and angle calibration. This leaves the actual sample temperature near T_N uncertain.
concerns.quote: the BMS laser power, spot size and estimated heating of a 220 nm absorbing film on SiO2; the cryostat and temperature sensor location

concerns.concern: The effect comes from a single flake with no repeat measurements or thermal cycling.
concerns.quote: The effect comes from a single flake at one q, with sparse temperature points and no repeat or cycling.

concerns.concern: The FEM model omits key parameters. These include the Si thickness (a fixed bottom can introduce spurious modes), cell length, substrate elastic constants and densities, NiPS3 density, and how the DFT tensor axes were rotated onto the propagation direction.
concerns.quote: The FEM description also omits the Si thickness ('represented numerically by a finite thickness', with a fixed bottom that can introduce spurious modes)

concerns.concern: Calling the effect 'giant' and 'rarely reported' overstates the evidence. Ultrasonic studies of bulk antiferromagnets routinely report elastic anomalies of a few percent at T_N.
concerns.quote: Labelling the effect 'giant' and unprecedented is therefore an overstatement at this stage.

concerns.concern: Identifying the b-axis from cleavage edges is not secure. The pseudo-hexagonal [100] and [110] edges are optically indistinguishable, so q may lie along a ±60° equivalent direction rather than b.
concerns.quote: An edge perpendicular to q could therefore correspond to b or to one of the ±60° pseudo-equivalent armchair directions.

concerns.concern: Exfoliated films typically host three zigzag magnetic domain orientations. The relation between q and the ferromagnetic chain direction is therefore not fixed, which matters for interpreting anisotropic elastic changes.
concerns.quote: exfoliated films typically host three magnetic domain orientations.

concerns.concern: The DFT supercell specification is ambiguous. The quoted dimensions do not match a 1×4×2 conventional or primitive cell, which hampers reproducibility of the elastic tensors.
concerns.quote: The quoted dimensions are close to 2×2×~2 conventional cells, not 1×4×2 of either the conventional or primitive cell.

concerns.concern: A ~10% gap between simulated (4.6 GHz) and measured (4.2 GHz) frequencies is described as 'close agreement'. This gap is larger than the magnetic effect under study.
concerns.quote: a ~10% discrepancy, larger than the magnetic effect under study, yet it is described as 'close agreement'.

concerns.concern: The experimental drop is inconsistently quoted as ~6% in one place and ~5.5% elsewhere.
concerns.quote: The text also inconsistently quotes the experimental drop as ~6% here and ~5.5% elsewhere.

concerns.concern: The Loudon surface-ripple selection rule is misstated. Intensity depends on the surface-normal displacement, not on any displacement perpendicular to propagation. Elasto-optic contributions in the absorbing film are also ignored.
concerns.quote: The surface-ripple mechanism of Loudon (ref. 42) gives an intensity proportional to the surface-normal displacement |u_z(0)|².

concerns.concern: The claim that all Raman-active modes are observed is overstated. There are 15 Raman-active modes, but only about 8–9 features are fitted, several of them unresolved Ag/Bg pairs.
concerns.quote: Fig. 1(c) shows about 8–9 fitted features, several labelled as unresolved Ag/Bg pairs, so not all modes are individually observed.

concerns.concern: Fig. 4(a) shows an 80 K spectrum that has no corresponding data point in Fig. 4(b).
concerns.quote: Fig. 4(a) also shows an 80 K spectrum with no corresponding point in Fig. 4(b).
